## Example 6.15 · Parts (a–b) {#iv6-example-6-15-ab .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .angles-lesson .a-dot-pair}

```{=html}
<p>For each pair of vectors, calculate <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}"></span> and <span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|"></span>. Hence determine whether the vectors are parallel in the same direction, parallel in opposite directions, or not parallel.</p><div class="a-cols "><div><p>a)</p><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}=2\underset{\sim}{i}-\underset{\sim}{j},\quad\underset{\sim}{b}=6\underset{\sim}{i}-3\underset{\sim}{j}."></span></div><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="a-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show (a)</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=2(6)+(-1)(-3)=15"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2}\sqrt{6^2+(-3)^2}=\sqrt5\sqrt{45}=15"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|"></span></div><p>Parallel in the same direction.</p></div></div></div><div><p>b)</p><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}=\underset{\sim}{i}+2\underset{\sim}{j}-2\underset{\sim}{k},\quad\underset{\sim}{b}=-2\underset{\sim}{i}-4\underset{\sim}{j}+4\underset{\sim}{k}."></span></div><div data-module="reveal-panel" class="a-reveal"><button class="toggle-panel" aria-pressed="false">Show (b)</button><div class="panel-answer" hidden><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=1(-2)+2(-4)+(-2)(4)=-18"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|=\sqrt{1+4+4}\sqrt{4+16+16}=3(6)=18"></span></div><div class="a-eq"><span data-math="\underset{\sim}{a}\cdot\underset{\sim}{b}=-|\underset{\sim}{a}||\underset{\sim}{b}|"></span></div><p>Parallel in opposite directions.</p></div></div></div></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Section 6 · p. 52</div>

::: notes
These are the same pairs as Example 6.11. Both methods must give the same classifications. In part (c), a positive dot product does not establish parallelism: 24 is neither 25 nor -25.
:::
